evidence_quotes: 16 earthquakes were recorded across Alaska's Aleutian region over the 30-day window
Magnitudes ranged from M4.0 to M6.2, with an average of M4.71
The M6.2 event near Nikolski on January 25
Nikolski, Alaska dominated the activity, accounting for 13 of 16 events (81%)
No tsunami alerts were issued for any event in this period
2 events on both Feb 14 and Feb 15
criticisms: The report describes the period as '30-day window' but the digest covers Jan 17 to Feb 16, which is exactly 30 days — this is acceptable, though the report says 'roughly one event every two days' (16 events / 30 days ≈ 0.53/day or one every ~1.9 days), which is a minor rounding approximation but not a fabrication.

The report characterizes the shallow follow-on sequence east of Nikolski as 'potential aftershock activity' — this is an interpretive framing not directly stated in the digest, but it is a reasonable inference from the data (M6.2 on Jan 25 followed by shallower events east of Nikolski) and does not constitute a fabricated fact.
The report says 'late-February acceleration in daily counts' when Feb 14-15 is technically mid-to-late February — a very minor characterization issue, not a factual error.

The claim that 'Several of these were extremely shallow (under 5 km depth)' is supported by the digest: events at 1.0 km, 1.4 km, 2.6 km, 3.3 km, and 5.8 km depth are all present in sample_events near Nikolski.
